links.outcome: Pre-analytical and analytical factors driving AI-pathologist TCC discrepancies
links.effect: Specimen type and cautery/crush artifacts were the main pre-analytical contributors to DQ-VQ discrepancies; specimen cellularity variation was the dominant analytical factor.
links.quote: Analysis of pre-analytical and analytical factors identified specimen type and cautery/crush artifacts as the main pre-analytical contributors to DQ-VQ discrepancies, while overall variations in specimen cellularity was the dominant analytical factor.

links.outcome: Agreement of AI and pathologist tumor cell content estimates with molecular quantification
links.effect: AI DQ showed stronger concordance with MQ (Rs = 0.63) than pathologist VQ with MQ (Spearman Rs = 0.38); VQ–DQ agreement was Rs = 0.44.
links.quote: Agreement was lowest between VQ and MQ (Spearman Rs = 0.38) and between VQ and DQ (Rs = 0.44), while DQ showed stronger concordance with MQ (Rs = 0.63).

links.effect: AI-based digital quantification showed stronger concordance (Rs = 0.63) than pathologists' visual quantification (Rs = 0.38).
links.quote: Agreement was lowest between VQ and MQ (Spearman Rs = 0.38) and between VQ and DQ (Rs = 0.44), while DQ showed stronger concordance with MQ (Rs = 0.63).

screen.reason: Empirical validation of an AI-based digital quantification tool on routine molecular pathology samples compared to manual visual quantification and molecular quantification, assessing analytical performance and artifact failure modes.
